question.problem:
| ** Production  $\,$ ($x$)** | **$24$** | **$27$** | **$30$** | **$31$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ** Price per $kg$  ($y$) ** | $2$ | $1.6$ | $1.4$ | $1.4$ |

The table above shows wheat production, in tons, and the average price of a kilogram of flour, in dollars, for a given country over the last four years. The corresponding linear regression line fitted using this sample is $\overset{^}{\,y}=4-0.1x.$
Assuming that all conditions for the simple regression model are satisfied, $\overset{―}{x}=28,$ and $\text{MSE}=0.007,$ find a $90%$ confidence interval for the slope of the regression line.   

*Hint: Use the fact that $P(T>2.92)=0.05,$ where $T$ has a student's $t$-distribution with $2$ degrees of freedom. Also, the standard error for the slope is given by* 

$$
\text{SE}[{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}\,]=\sqrt{\frac{\text{MSE}}{{S}_{xx}}}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
We use the following notations:

- $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ is the regression line that best fits the population, and

- $\overset{^}{\,y}={\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0}+{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}x$ is the estimate of the "true" regression line given by the data in our sample.

In this case, we have that  

$$
\overset{^}{\,y}={\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{0}+{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}x=-4-0.1x.
$$

We are told that all assumptions for a simple regression model are held. So, given a value $\alpha $ between $0$ and $1,$ the corresponding $[100(1-\alpha )]%$ confidence interval for the slope ${\beta }_{1}$ of our model can be written as

$$
{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}\,\pm \,\overset{\text{margin of error}}{\overset{⏞}{{t}_{n-2,\alpha /2}\cdot \text{SE}[{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}\,]}}.
$$

Note the following:

- $\,{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}$ is our point estimate for the slope, computed using the data points from our sample.

- $P(T>{t}_{n-2,\alpha /2})=\frac{\alpha }{2},$ where $T$ has a student's $t$-distribution with $n-2$ degrees of freedom.

- $\text{SE}[{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}\,]$ is the standard error of ${\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1},$ given by

$$
\text{SE}[{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}\,]=\sqrt{\frac{\text{MSE}}{{S}_{xx}}}
$$

where we have:

- $\text{MSE}$ is the mean squared error of the model:

$$
\text{MSE}=\frac{1}{n-2}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({y}_{i}-{\overset{^}{\,y}}_{i})^{2}
$$

where ${\overset{^}{\,y}}_{i}$ is the estimate of ${y}_{i}$ given by our regression model.

- ${S}_{xx}$ is the usual sum of squares formula:

$$
{S}_{xx}={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}
$$

To construct the confidence interval, we proceed as follows:

- **Step 1.** Find the point estimate. From the regression equation $\overset{^}{\,y}=4-0.1x,$ our point estimate is

$$
{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}=-0.1.
$$

- **Step 2.** Find the margin of error. 

- Since we are interested in finding a $90%$ confidence interval, we have 

$$
\alpha =1-0.9=0.1\,⟹\,\frac{\alpha }{2}=0.05.
$$

We are given that $P(T>2.92)=0.05.$ As a result, 

$$
{t}_{n-2,\alpha /2}={t}_{2,0.05}=2.92.
$$

- Computing ${S}_{xx},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} & =(24-28)^{2}+(27-28)^{2}+(30-28)^{2}+(31-28)^{2} \\  & =16+1+4+9 \\  & =30.\end{aligned}
$$

- Now, we can compute the margin of error:

$$
{t}_{n-2,\alpha /2}\cdot \text{SE}[{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}\,]=2.92\cdot \sqrt{\frac{0.007}{30}}≈0.04
$$

- **Step 3.** Determine the limits of the confidence interval:

$$
{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}\,\pm \,{t}_{n-2,\alpha /2}\cdot \text{SE}[{\overset{^}{\,\beta }}_{1}\,]=-0.1\pm 0.04
$$
